answer_1.quote: we first design three types of evidence pollution methods ( §2): (i) basic evidence pollution that manipulate evidence without LLMs; (ii) rephrase evidence that prompts LLMs to rewrite existing evidence; and (iii) generated evidence that directly prompts LLMs to generate fictional evidence
answer_1.outputs: manipulated evidence such as rephrased or generated social media comments

answer_2.quote: We employ SimCSE to evaluate the relevance between social text and corresponding evidence and employ BERTscore and ROUGE-L to evaluate the semantic-level and word-level similarity between original and rephrased evidence

answer_4.quote: We recruit 99 annotators familiar with social networking platforms to judge which comment is of higher quality for a certain social text.
answer_4.guideline: Thank you for attending our human evaluation. Social media users would comment on a post to express their opinions. You are asked to check which comment is of higher quality for a certain post (comment 1 or 2). Please consider factors such as relevance to the post, tone, suitability for the social platform (for the use of hashtags), etc. Please do not consider the length and grammatical errors of the comment. If you think two comments are of equal quality, please subjectively choose the one you like.
